title: What happens after you apply for Adult Disability Payment in Scotland?
scope: Scotland, new applications for Adult Disability Payment
reader: An applicant or adviser who wants to know how a new claim is decided, what makes it take longer and how to challenge a decision.
primaryAngle: Follow the two parts of a new application, supporting information, a determination, and re-determination and appeal where the applicant disagrees.
secondaryAngle: Show which part of the journey the published processing measure covers, how routes and outcomes differ, and how Audit Scotland judged delivery.
lastingValue: Applicants need a clear sequence and realistic time measures regardless of the release cycle.

signals.detail: The published application and re-determination routes create recurring questions about evidence, waiting and how to challenge a decision.
The July 2026 statistics, published 15 September, give a recent baseline with linked tables and supplementary analyses.

apply.title: How to apply for Adult Disability Payment
apply.locator: Part 1, part 2, supporting information and the decision.

redetermination.title: Requesting a re-determination or an appeal
redetermination.locator: Application to Social Security Scotland and appeal route. Check eligibility and time limits in force.

july-figures.title: Adult Disability Payment statistics to 31 July 2026
july-figures.locator: New applications, processing times, outcomes and linked tables, including supplementary authorisation rates.

audit-report.title: Adult Disability Payment
audit-report.locator: Performance audit, application design, implementation, timings and funding. Distinguish report-period estimates from current forecasts.

forthcoming.title: Forthcoming publications
forthcoming.locator: Check the next Adult Disability Payment publication date and whether a newer release has superseded July 2026.

usefulness.reason: The decision and any challenge have clear consequences for a person’s income.

urgency.reason: The quarterly release gives a current baseline. There is no immediate release or policy deadline recorded in this brief.

coverage.reason: Adds a Scottish benefit and separates a new disability claim from the existing Carer’s Allowance debt guide.

evidence.reason: Current application guidance, official statistics and an independent audit cover the service and how it operates.

evidenceGap: A processing time starting after part 2 leaves out time spent on the initial application. Check whether a linked cohort measure covers receipt of part 1 through decision and first payment.
draftingChecks: Keep transfers from Personal Independence Payment, new applications and special rules cases identifiable. Check which are included in each published figure before comparing time or approval rates.
Identify the date each measure starts and ends and what the figures say about long waits. Read an appropriate case or audit passage for a documented consequence.
Trace the most relevant audit recommendations and later evidence. Separate benefit payments, case administration and estimated funding gaps.

nextCheck.what: Check the latest and forthcoming publications for a newer release and review any updated audit follow-up.

decisionReason: The main process, measurement issue and delivery evidence are sufficient for a standalone draft.
